title: China's AI Export Boom Makes Beijing Less Afraid of Stronger Yuan — AI-Driven Revenue Powers Sixth Consecutive Quarterly Gain Against Dollar
detail: The global surge in demand for Chinese AI products — AI models, cloud services, hardware, and AI-supercharged manufactured goods — is changing Beijing's traditional calculus on yuan management, Bloomberg reported on May 28. The onshore yuan is on track for a sixth consecutive quarterly gain against the US dollar, a streak last seen in 2013, as AI-linked exports power Chinese export earnings at scale. Bloomberg's analysis frames this as a structural shift: China historically tolerated or engineered yuan weakness to boost export competitiveness, but the high value-add nature of AI exports (which compete on capability rather than price) means a stronger yuan no longer carries the same risk of eroding export market share. The analysis builds directly on Bloomberg's May 12 finding that China earns $500M per hour from AI-supercharged exports — with AI hardware and semiconductors comprising approximately 50% of China's export growth acceleration (Goldman Sachs/Nomura estimates). The yuan's strengthening is also supported by China's April 2026 trade data: exports +14.1% YoY (consensus: +7.1%) and imports +25.3% YoY (consensus: +16.1%), both massive beats against expectations. The shift has strategic significance beyond currency markets: a stronger yuan reduces the import cost of the critical equipment and materials China still sources internationally (semiconductor raw materials, specialty chemicals, Western precision instruments below export control thresholds), while the AI export revenue stream reduces vulnerability to rare-earth export-for-chip-access leverage scenarios. The May 12, 2026 US-China trade truce (tariffs from 145% to 30% baseline) and May 14-15 Trump-Xi summit provided additional stability; China appears to be entering a phase where AI export earnings structurally reduce its incentive to engage in competitive currency depreciation — a reversal from the 2018-2019 trade war dynamics.

title: China's Cheap Energy Infrastructure as Structural AI Advantage — 60 GW Data Center Expansion by 2030, Double US Electricity Generation Capacity
detail: China's massive energy infrastructure is emerging as a structural competitive advantage in the global AI race, Al Jazeera reported in an investigative analysis on May 28. China generates more than twice the electricity of the United States annually and is set to double its data center capacity by 2030, with 28 GW of new data center projects coming online to add to the 32 GW already installed — reaching approximately 60 GW total by 2030. Data center rack count grew at approximately 30% annually between 2016 and 2023. China's energy cost advantage directly affects AI compute economics: running AI inference and training workloads on Chinese domestic data center infrastructure costs significantly less per token than equivalent US capacity, due to a combination of cheap coal and hydroelectric power in key provinces (Inner Mongolia, Guizhou, Sichuan) and state-subsidized electricity pricing for strategic AI infrastructure. The energy advantage compounds China's other compute cost advantages: DeepSeek V3's architecture-level training efficiency (2.788M H800 GPU-hours for ~$5.6M) and the permanent 75% price cut on V4 Pro API ($0.003625/M tokens, below Western rivals' estimated compute cost per Semafor) together with cheap energy mean Chinese AI infrastructure can serve global API demand at structurally lower costs than US equivalents. Al Jazeera notes that Western AI providers — constrained by expensive US grid electricity, data center power costs in the $0.08-0.15/kWh range versus China's $0.03-0.06/kWh — face a compute cost disadvantage that compounds over time as AI inference workloads scale. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) explicitly includes accelerating data center electrification and clean energy integration for AI infrastructure, with multiple provinces offering preferential electricity pricing for AI companies meeting government-aligned development criteria.
